patient.chief_complaint: Confusion and unresponsiveness following brief convulsion 35 minutes ago, history of recent cardiac arrest
patient.hpi: A 55-year-old White female accountant was brought to the emergency department by her husband after a brief generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home. The husband reports she convulsed for approximately 2 minutes and had not returned to her baseline level of alertness 35 minutes later. He was instructed to call 911. Critical history: the patient suffered a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation 5 days ago. She was resuscitated after approximately 12 minutes of cardiac arrest (time from collapse to ROSC), intubated in the field, and was admitted to the cardiac ICU where she underwent targeted temperature management (TTM, 33°C for 24 hours) followed by controlled rewarming. She was extubated on day 3 and was discharged home on day 4 — somewhat prematurely in retrospect — with a newly implanted ICD. Since discharge she has been confused, more than expected, with prominent short-term memory impairment and episodes where she 'stares into space.' Her husband noted she had several brief 'staring spells' at home over the past 24 hours before today's convulsion. She takes aspirin, atorvastatin, and amiodarone following the cardiac arrest. Her husband reports the 'staring spells' were not recognized as seizures at discharge. No fever. No headache. No new cardiac symptoms. She was told post-cardiac arrest cognitive changes are 'normal' at discharge. Family history: mother with coronary artery disease. No epilepsy.

eeg.impression: ABNORMAL EEG. Non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) superimposed on post-anoxic encephalopathy background. GPDs with ictal runs meeting NCSE criteria. In the context of recent cardiac arrest with 12-minute resuscitation time, urgent IV benzodiazepine trial is indicated. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 108 mg/dL (H), Troponin I (high sensitivity) 0.24 ng/mL (H), BNP 486 pg/mL (H), NSE (neuron-specific enolase) 42 mcg/L (H).
abnormal_values_summary: NSE 42 mcg/L (markedly elevated) — significant post-anoxic neuronal injury

ct.impression: Diffuse subtle gray-white matter loss of differentiation with sulcal effacement — consistent with diffuse hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy from recent cardiac arrest. No new hemorrhage. CT underestimates extent of anoxic injury — MRI with DWI required for prognostication.
recommended_actions: MRI brain with DWI/ADC at minimum 72h post-arrest for accurate prognosis (earlier may underestimate injury)
Continuous EEG for 48-72 hours for NCSE monitoring and prognostication
NSE at 48 and 72 hours post-arrest for prognostication

findings.location: bilateral cortex — watershed zones, basal ganglia, thalami

output.impression: Extensive diffuse hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). Bilateral cortical watershed and basal ganglia DWI restriction with ADC reduction — cortical laminar necrosis. Bilateral hippocampal involvement. Clinical correlation recommended.

Post-anoxic NCSE with progressive EEG deterioration. Evolution to burst-suppression with GPDs — poor prognostic pattern in post-cardiac arrest NCSE. Combined with extensive DWI restriction on MRI and NSE 42 mcg/L — multimodal prognostication supports very poor neurological outcome. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions.description: Lacosamide prolongs PR interval via sodium channel blockade; amiodarone also prolongs PR interval and QTc. Combination increases risk of PR prolongation and AV block.
interactions.clinical_recommendation: Prefer levetiracetam over lacosamide for NCSE in patients on amiodarone. If lacosamide is used, obtain baseline ECG and monitor for PR prolongation and AV block.

interactions.description: No significant interaction between amiodarone and levetiracetam
interactions.clinical_recommendation: Levetiracetam is safe with amiodarone — preferred AED choice in this patient

output.summary: Amiodarone + lacosamide = additive PR prolongation risk — prefer levetiracetam. Levetiracetam is safe with amiodarone and has no cardiac conduction effects.

output.methodology: Bilateral median nerve stimulation; recording from C3-Fz and C4-Fz; N20 cortical response evaluated

results.interpretation: Bilateral absent N20 cortical responses — indicates failure of cortical signal transmission. Per AAN guidelines, bilateral absent SSEPs at >24h post-cardiac arrest with 100% specificity (0% false positive rate) for predicting poor neurological outcome (death or vegetative state) when using TTM protocol.

output.impression: Bilateral absent N20 SSEP responses — highest-level predictor of poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest. Combined with MRI (extensive bilateral cortical DWI restriction), NSE >33 mcg/L, and post-anoxic NCSE with burst-suppression evolution, multimodal assessment confirms very poor prognosis. Goals-of-care discussion with family essential.
recommended_actions: Goals of care family meeting — consider comfort-focused care
Consider organ donation discussion if family consents
Continue AED and supportive care proportionate to family wishes and goals

results.title: Neuroprognostication after cardiac arrest: systematic review and meta-analysis
results.key_finding: Multimodal neuroprognostication: bilateral absent SSEPs (specificity 100%), NSE >33 mcg/L at 48-72h (specificity >90%), extensive bilateral cortical DWI restriction on MRI, and malignant EEG patterns (burst-suppression, suppression) together predict very poor neurological outcome (death/VS) with near 100% specificity. Post-anoxic NCSE alone is not invariably fatal but combined with other markers indicates poor prognosis.

output.summary: Post-anoxic NCSE: treatment should continue while prognosis is uncertain. Multimodal approach (EEG + MRI + SSEP + NSE) provides highest diagnostic accuracy for neuroprognostication. Bilateral absent SSEPs + extensive DWI restriction + NSE >33 + malignant EEG = very poor outcome with near 100% specificity.

contraindicated_actions: Lacosamide in patient on amiodarone — additive PR prolongation and AV block risk
Premature prognostication within first 24-48 hours before full multimodal assessment
Aggressive AED escalation to burst-suppression induction in post-anoxic NCSE with multimodal poor prognosis — may mask natural EEG evolution without benefit
key_reasoning_points: Post-anoxic NCSE following cardiac arrest requires simultaneous seizure treatment AND neuroprognostication
Amiodarone + lacosamide = additive PR prolongation — levetiracetam is the safe AED choice
Bilateral absent SSEPs (N20) at >24h post-arrest with TTM = 100% specificity for poor outcome (no false positives)
NSE >33 mcg/L at 48-72h post-arrest with TTM = >90% specificity for poor outcome
Multimodal neuroprognostication required — no single marker is sufficient; must combine EEG + MRI + SSEP + NSE
Early discharge from cardiac ICU (day 4) was premature — 'staring spells' at home were likely NCSE events that were not recognized

metadata.clinical_pearl: Post-cardiac arrest NCSE: amiodarone + lacosamide = PR block risk — use levetiracetam. Prognosticate with bilateral SSEPs + NSE + MRI DWI + EEG pattern — all four before any goals-of-care decision.
